title: Decoding Naturalistic Speech from fMRI with Temporal Modeling and Multimodal Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2610.22049v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reconstructing what a person perceives from their brain activity is a stringent test of whether neural recordings carry meaningful information. Naturalistic speech offers a rich testbed for this challenge: it unfolds over multiple timescales, but fMRI's noisy, temporally smeared measurements make this structure hard to recover. We introduce NOEMA, a temporal convolutional decoder that aligns windows of consecutive fMRI measurements with multimodal stimulus embeddings. These embeddings combine complementary text, audio, and speech representations of the same stimulus segment, enabling its retrieval directly from brain activity. On two naturalistic speech datasets, Cephalonauts One and LeBel, NOEMA retrieves the correct segment among 2,000 candidates within the top 10 for more than 42% of held-out queries. translated_title: 基于时间建模与多模态对齐的fMRI自然语音解码
translated_abstract: 从大脑活动中重建一个人所感知的内容，是检验神经记录是否携带有意义信息的严格测试。自然语音为这一挑战提供了丰富的测试平台：它在多个时间尺度上展开，但fMRI含噪且时间上模糊的测量使得这种结构难以恢复。我们提出了NOEMA，一个时间卷积解码器，它将连续fMRI测量的时间窗口与多模态刺激嵌入对齐。这些嵌入结合了同一刺激片段的互补的文本、音频和语音表征，使其能够直接从大脑活动中被检索。在两个自然语音数据集Cephalonauts One和LeBel上，NOEMA在超过42%的保留查询中，从2,000个候选片段中于前10名内检索出正确的片段。这显著优于基线解码器，并且当候选池扩展到数千个干扰项时，这一优势依然保持。
tldr: 提出NOEMA时间卷积解码器，通过将连续fMRI测量与多模态（文本、音频、语音）刺激嵌入对齐，实现了从大脑活动中高精度检索自然语音片段，在2000个候选中前10命中率超过42%。
en_tdlr: NOEMA, a temporal convolutional decoder aligning consecutive fMRI measurements with multimodal stimulus embeddings combining text, audio, and speech representations, achieves accurate retrieval of naturalistic speech segments from brain activity, ranking the correct segment in the top 10 out of 2,000 candidates for over 42% of queries.
